$comment: Thresholds enforced by the scheduled load-test workflow (issue #735).
These are DELIBERATE thresholds, not a recorded run: they are derived from
the local reference baselines in docs/PERFORMANCE.md (worst row per
endpoint) and then relaxed, because shared CI runners are slower and noisier
• p95Ms / p99Ms  — multiplied by LOAD_TEST_MARGIN (margin.default below,
overridable per workflow_dispatch run). Latency scales
with runner hardware, so it gets a multiplier.
• errorPct       — absolute cap on transport errors per connection.
• non2xxPct      — absolute cap on 4xx/5xx responses (null = n/a for SSE).
To change a gate on purpose, edit the value here AND explain it in the PR
body. Never raise a threshold to silence a real regression — see

margin.rationale: CI runner latency for the same code is 2-5x the local reference run; 3x keeps genuine 2x+ regressions visible without flaking on a slow runner.

/api/health.note: Worst documented row is 50 connections (p95 503ms / p99 1211ms). Health does a DB SELECT 1 plus RPC/Horizon/Redis pings, so it is the noisiest endpoint.

/api/payments.note: Worst documented row is 50 connections (p95 847ms / p99 2103ms). Authenticated: a non-zero non-2xx rate means the API key is missing or wrong.

/api/events.note: SSE streams never complete a request, so req/s, latency and non-2xx are n/a. Only transport errors (a failed stream open) are gated; connection leaks and heartbeat timing are asserted by scripts/sse-load-test.mjs itself.
